Including revenue from the 2012, 2017 and 2023 reissues, *Titanic* earned $674.3 million in North America and $1.583 billion in other countries, for a worldwide total of $2.257 billion.[Note 1][14] It became the highest-grossing film of all time worldwide in 1998, beating *Jurassic Park* (1993).[105] The film remained so for twelve years, until *Avatar* (2009), also written and directed by Cameron, surpassed it in 2010.[106] On March 1, 1998,[107] it became the first film to earn more than $1 billion worldwide[108] and on the weekend April 13–15, 2012—a century after the original vessel's foundering, *Titanic* became the second film to cross the $2 billion threshold during its 3D re-release.[109] Box Office Mojo estimates that *Titanic* is the fifth-highest-grossing film of all time in North America when adjusting for ticket price inflation.[110] The site also estimates that the film sold over 128 million tickets in the US in its initial theatrical run.[111]

Its highest grossing single day was Saturday, February 14, 1998, on which it earned $13,048,711, more than eight weeks after its North American debut.[117][118] On March 14, it surpassed *Star Wars* as the highest-grossing film ever in North America.[119] It stayed at number one for 15 consecutive weeks in North America, a record for any film.[120] By April 1998, the film's number one spot would be overtaken by *Lost in Space*, dropping into second place.[121] The film stayed in theaters in North America for almost 10 months before finally closing on Thursday, October 1, 1998, with a final domestic gross of $600,788,188,[122] equivalent to $1140.3  million in 2023[123]. Outside North America, the film made double its North American gross, generating $1,242,413,080[124] and accumulating a grand total of $1,843,201,268 worldwide from its initial theatrical run.[125]

The Numbers does not log individual releases, but had the lifetime total recorded as $2.186 billion in September 2014 (roughly equating to $1.843 billion for the original release and $343.6 million for the 3D reissue).[11] A couple of weeks later, The Numbers increased the lifetime gross to $2.208 billion, without explanation.[12] Prior to the 2023 re-release, the totals at both trackers were inflated above the true figure. For clarity, *Titanic* earned $1.843 billion on its original release, $344 million from its 2012 reissue, $691,642 from the 2017 reissue, and $71,352 in 2020, for a lifetime total of $2,187,687,082 from the first four releases. Along with the $70.2 million grossed from the 25th anniversary re-release in 2023,[13] the lifetime total for *Titanic* stands at $2,257,844,554 as of May 22, 2023[update].

**James Cameron – Director with the second‑largest career worldwide box‑office gross (≈ $8.7 billion)**  

Below are all of the feature‑length films that James Cameron is credited as director (commercial theatrical releases).  The production‑budget figures are taken from the films’ Wikipedia “Budget” infoboxes (or, where Wikipedia cites another reliable source, that source is noted).  All amounts are expressed in U.S. dollars and rounded to the nearest million.

| Year | Film (Director) | Production budget (USD) | Source |
|------|-----------------|--------------------------|--------|
| 1984 | **The Terminator** | **$6 million** | Wikipedia – “The Terminator” (budget $6 M) |
| 1986 | **Aliens** | **$18 million** | Wikipedia – “Aliens” (budget $18 M) |
| 1989 | **The Abyss** | **$70 million** | Wikipedia – “The Abyss” (budget $70 M) |
| 1991 | **Terminator 2: Judgment Day** | **$102 million** | Wikipedia – “Terminator 2: Judgment Day” (budget $102 M) |
| 1994 | **True Lies** | **$100 million** | Wikipedia – “True Lies” (budget $100 M) |
| 1997 | **Titanic** | **$200 million** | Wikipedia – “Titanic (1997 film)” (budget $200 M) |
| 2009 | **Avatar** | **$237 million** | Wikipedia – “Avatar (2009 film)” (budget $237 M) |
| 2022 | **Avatar: The Way of Water** | **$350 million** (estimated) | Wikipedia – “Avatar: The Way of Water” (budget $350 M [estimated]) |

**Notes & caveats**

* Budgets are the *production* costs reported in the infoboxes; they do **not** include marketing, distribution, or post‑release expenses.  
* For *Avatar: The Way of Water* the exact figure has not been officially disclosed; industry reports and the Wikipedia page cite an estimated production cost in the **$350 – $460 million** range. The lower end ($350 M) is shown here for consistency.  
* Earlier works such as *Piranha II: The Spawning* (1990) were co‑directed by Cameron but he is not universally credited as the primary director; they are omitted to keep the list to films where Cameron is the sole credited director.  

These eight films constitute James Cameron’s complete theatrical directing oeuvre and together account for the bulk of his $8.7 billion worldwide box‑office tally, placing him second only to Steven Spielberg on the “highest‑grossing film directors” list.
